**W15**: "Again the cold chill seized Tommy" — "again" is a callback dangle; the prior instance of the cold chill is not in this window. Also "Hence the sealed envelope—bait" — "the sealed envelope" is a definite-article dangle with no introduction in this window.

**W16**: "Hence the sealed envelope—bait" — same definite-article dangle.

**W18**: "He clutched Albert" — the "He" opens the window with no antecedent established inside it (pronoun dangle). Also connective dangle: the singing instruction follows something not in this window.

**W19**: Opens mid-song with no setup inside the window — connective dangle.

**W21**: "In Tuppence's hospital days the gramophone had ground it out a hundred times" — "it" refers to the song not present in this window (definite-article/pronoun dangle). Also the paragraph opens as if following directly from something not shown.

**W26**: Opens with "He repeated it, abashed" — pronoun dangle ("He") and "it" refers to something said not in this window.

**W33**: Opens with dialogue and action ("Pack my bag!") that follows a note whose content is not in this window — connective/definite-article dangle on "the note."

**W34**: "He smoothed the note thoughtfully" — "the note" is a definite-article dangle; "some one else" and "who it is" are callback dangles with no antecedent in the window.

**W32**: "Yours, TWOPENCE." opens the window — the letter body is not in this window, making this a connective/definite-article dangle.

**W25**: Opens with "He repeated it, abashed" — pronoun and "it" dangle.
